The only India-side trace is the import footprint itself: 94 inbound customs records with 12 observed port lanes ("Top Ports: MUNDRA SEA 11, Haiphong 8, Sokhna 5, Singapore 4, CHENNAI SEA 4"), which proves the company actively operates a mineral-processing business in India (limestone lumps, calcite powder, grinding-mill spares) but is not evidence of domestic sales.
note: IMPORTANT ENTITY DISAMBIGUATION: the ImportKey slug /gayatri-microns (14 records, FB 62 E MIA ALWAR, Rajasthan) is a DIFFERENT company — 'GAYATRI MICRONS', not 'GAYATRI MICRONS LIMITED'. Its export rows (e.g. "2025-04-28 | GAYATRI MICRONS | DHAULAGIRI MICRO MINERALS PVT LTD | CALCITE POWDER 2 MIC | Sonauli LCS, India | Bhairawa, NEPAL | 25309030 | BOL 1324274") must NOT be attributed to this supplier; they are recorded here only to document that they were checked and excluded. For GAYATRI MICRONS LIMITED itself: import activity is confirmed and current (latest record 2026-02-26), so the company is real and trading, but no dated export bill of lading and no domestic supply record was found in accessible sources. HS code note: declared HS 251741 (granules/chippings of marble) does not match the observed trade — actual codes seen are 25210090 (limestone), 25309030 (calcite), 38249900 (coated calcite) and 84749000 (mill spares); per project rules this is not a rejection ground, the code should be corrected to the factual one. Revenue and export volume: null — not public in the sources reachable. No CIN/PAN verified. Verdict: real operating company, shipments factual on the import side only; export and domestic supply status remain 'declared, not confirmed' — traces of outbound supply to Kuwait exist only as counterparty listings without shipment detail.
